doc.md:
Makes its child scrollable.

It does so using either internally added scrollbars or externally
associated adjustments, and optionally draws a frame around the child.

Widgets with native scrolling support, i.e. those whose classes implement
the [`Scrollable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Scrollable) interface, are added directly. For other types
of widget, the class [`Viewport`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Viewport) acts as an adaptor, giving
scrollability to other widgets. [`ScrolledWindow.set_child()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:set_child)
intelligently accounts for whether or not the added child is a `GtkScrollable`.
If it isn’t, then it wraps the child in a `GtkViewport`. Therefore, you can
just add any child widget and not worry about the details.

If [`ScrolledWindow.set_child()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:set_child) has added a `GtkViewport` for you,
it will be automatically removed when you unset the child.
Unless [`ScrolledWindow:hscrollbar-policy`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:hscrollbar-policy) and
[`ScrolledWindow:vscrollbar-policy`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:vscrollbar-policy) are %GTK_POLICY_NEVER or
%GTK_POLICY_EXTERNAL, `GtkScrolledWindow` adds internal `GtkScrollbar` widgets
around its child. The scroll position of the child, and if applicable the
scrollbars, is controlled by the [`ScrolledWindow:hadjustment`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:hadjustment)
and [`ScrolledWindow:vadjustment`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:vadjustment) that are associated with the
`GtkScrolledWindow`. See the docs on [`Scrollbar`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Scrollbar) for the details,
but note that the “step_increment” and “page_increment” fields are only
effective if the policy causes scrollbars to be present.

If a `GtkScrolledWindow` doesn’t behave quite as you would like, or
doesn’t have exactly the right layout, it’s very possible to set up
your own scrolling with `GtkScrollbar` and for example a `GtkGrid`.

# Touch support

`GtkScrolledWindow` has built-in support for touch devices. When a
touchscreen is used, swiping will move the scrolled window, and will
expose 'kinetic' behavior. This can be turned off with the
[`ScrolledWindow:kinetic-scrolling`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:kinetic-scrolling) property if it is undesired.

`GtkScrolledWindow` also displays visual 'overshoot' indication when
the content is pulled beyond the end, and this situation can be
captured with the [`ScrolledWindow::edge-overshot`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#event:edge-overshot) signal.

If no mouse device is present, the scrollbars will overlaid as
narrow, auto-hiding indicators over the content. If traditional
scrollbars are desired although no mouse is present, this behaviour
can be turned off with the [`ScrolledWindow:overlay-scrolling`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:overlay-scrolling)
property.

# Shortcuts and Gestures

The following signals have default keybindings:

- [`ScrolledWindow::scroll-child`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#event:scroll-child)

# CSS nodes

`GtkScrolledWindow` has a main CSS node with name scrolledwindow.
It gets a .frame style class added when [`ScrolledWindow:has-frame`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:has-frame)
is `TRUE`.

It uses subnodes with names overshoot and undershoot to draw the overflow
and underflow indications. These nodes get the .left, .right, .top or .bottom
style class added depending on where the indication is drawn.

`GtkScrolledWindow` also sets the positional style classes (.left, .right,
.top, .bottom) and style classes related to overlay scrolling
(.overlay-indicator, .dragging, .hovering) on its scrollbars.

If both scrollbars are visible, the area where they meet is drawn
with a subnode named junction.

# Accessibility

Until GTK 4.10, `GtkScrolledWindow` used the [`AccessibleRole.group`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:group) role.

Starting from GTK 4.12, `GtkScrolledWindow` uses the [`AccessibleRole.generic`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:generic)
role.

get_child.md:
Gets the child widget of `scrolled_window`.

If the scrolled window automatically added a [`Viewport`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Viewport), this
function will return the viewport widget, and you can retrieve its child
using [`Viewport.get_child()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Viewport#method:get_child).

get_hadjustment.md:
Returns the horizontal scrollbar’s adjustment.

This is the adjustment used to connect the horizontal scrollbar
to the child widget’s horizontal scroll functionality.

get_has_frame.brief: Gets whether the scrolled window draws a frame.
get_has_frame.md: Gets whether the scrolled window draws a frame.

get_kinetic_scrolling.brief: Returns the specified kinetic scrolling behavior.
get_kinetic_scrolling.md: Returns the specified kinetic scrolling behavior.

get_max_content_height.brief: Returns the maximum content height set.
get_max_content_height.md: Returns the maximum content height set.

get_max_content_width.brief: Returns the maximum content width set.
get_max_content_width.md: Returns the maximum content width set.

get_min_content_height.brief: Gets the minimal content height of `scrolled_window`.
get_min_content_height.md: Gets the minimal content height of `scrolled_window`.

get_min_content_width.brief: Gets the minimum content width of `scrolled_window`.
get_min_content_width.md: Gets the minimum content width of `scrolled_window`.

get_overlay_scrolling.brief: Returns whether overlay scrolling is enabled for this scrolled window.
get_overlay_scrolling.md: Returns whether overlay scrolling is enabled for this scrolled window.

get_placement.brief: Gets the placement of the contents with respect to the scrollbars.
get_placement.md: Gets the placement of the contents with respect to the scrollbars.

get_policy.brief: Retrieves the current policy values for the horizontal and vertical scrollbars.
get_policy.md:
Retrieves the current policy values for the horizontal and vertical
scrollbars.

See [`ScrolledWindow.set_policy()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:set_policy).

get_propagate_natural_height.brief: Reports whether the natural height of the child will be calculated and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural height.
get_propagate_natural_height.md:
Reports whether the natural height of the child will be calculated
and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural height.

get_propagate_natural_width.brief: Reports whether the natural width of the child will be calculated and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural width.
get_propagate_natural_width.md:
Reports whether the natural width of the child will be calculated
and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural width.

get_vadjustment.md:
Returns the vertical scrollbar’s adjustment.

This is the adjustment used to connect the vertical
scrollbar to the child widget’s vertical scroll functionality.

set_child.md:
Sets the child widget of `scrolled_window`.

If `child` does not implement the [`Scrollable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Scrollable) interface,
the scrolled window will add `child` to a [`Viewport`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Viewport) instance
and then add the viewport as its child widget.

set_hadjustment.brief: Sets the `GtkAdjustment` for the horizontal scrollbar.
set_hadjustment.md: Sets the `GtkAdjustment` for the horizontal scrollbar.

set_has_frame.brief: Changes the frame drawn around the contents of `scrolled_window`.
set_has_frame.md: Changes the frame drawn around the contents of `scrolled_window`.

set_kinetic_scrolling.brief: Turns kinetic scrolling on or off.
set_kinetic_scrolling.md:
Turns kinetic scrolling on or off.

Kinetic scrolling only applies to devices with source
%GDK_SOURCE_TOUCHSCREEN.

set_max_content_height.brief: Sets the maximum height that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.
set_max_content_height.md:
Sets the maximum height that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.

The `scrolled_window` will grow up to this height before it starts
scrolling the content.

It is a programming error to set the maximum content height to a value
smaller than [`ScrolledWindow:min-content-height`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:min-content-height).

set_max_content_width.brief: Sets the maximum width that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.
set_max_content_width.md:
Sets the maximum width that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.

The `scrolled_window` will grow up to this width before it starts
scrolling the content.

It is a programming error to set the maximum content width to a
value smaller than [`ScrolledWindow:min-content-width`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:min-content-width).

set_min_content_height.brief: Sets the minimum height that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.
set_min_content_height.md:
Sets the minimum height that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.

Note that this can and (usually will) be smaller than the minimum
size of the content.

It is a programming error to set the minimum content height to a
value greater than [`ScrolledWindow:max-content-height`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:max-content-height).

set_min_content_width.brief: Sets the minimum width that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.
set_min_content_width.md:
Sets the minimum width that `scrolled_window` should keep visible.

Note that this can and (usually will) be smaller than the minimum
size of the content.

It is a programming error to set the minimum content width to a
value greater than [`ScrolledWindow:max-content-width`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#property:max-content-width).

set_overlay_scrolling.brief: Enables or disables overlay scrolling for this scrolled window.
set_overlay_scrolling.md: Enables or disables overlay scrolling for this scrolled window.

set_placement.brief: Sets the placement of the contents with respect to the scrollbars for the scrolled window.
set_placement.md:
Sets the placement of the contents with respect to the scrollbars
for the scrolled window.

The default is %GTK_CORNER_TOP_LEFT, meaning the child is
in the top left, with the scrollbars underneath and to the right.
Other values in [`CornerType`](xref:gtk:Gtk.CornerType) are %GTK_CORNER_TOP_RIGHT,
%GTK_CORNER_BOTTOM_LEFT, and %GTK_CORNER_BOTTOM_RIGHT.

See also [`ScrolledWindow.get_placement()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:get_placement) and
[`ScrolledWindow.unset_placement()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:unset_placement).

set_policy.brief: Sets the scrollbar policy for the horizontal and vertical scrollbars.
set_policy.md:
Sets the scrollbar policy for the horizontal and vertical scrollbars.

The policy determines when the scrollbar should appear; it is a value
from the [`PolicyType`](xref:gtk:Gtk.PolicyType) enumeration. If %GTK_POLICY_ALWAYS, the
scrollbar is always present; if %GTK_POLICY_NEVER, the scrollbar is
never present; if %GTK_POLICY_AUTOMATIC, the scrollbar is present only
if needed (that is, if the slider part of the bar would be smaller
than the trough — the display is larger than the page size).

set_propagate_natural_height.brief: Sets whether the natural height of the child should be calculated and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural height.
set_propagate_natural_height.md:
Sets whether the natural height of the child should be calculated
and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural height.

set_propagate_natural_width.brief: Sets whether the natural width of the child should be calculated and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural width.
set_propagate_natural_width.md:
Sets whether the natural width of the child should be calculated
and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural width.

set_vadjustment.brief: Sets the `GtkAdjustment` for the vertical scrollbar.
set_vadjustment.md: Sets the `GtkAdjustment` for the vertical scrollbar.

unset_placement.brief: Unsets the placement of the contents with respect to the scrollbars.
unset_placement.md:
Unsets the placement of the contents with respect to the scrollbars.

If no window placement is set for a scrolled window,
it defaults to %GTK_CORNER_TOP_LEFT.

child.md:
The child widget.

When setting this property, if the child widget does not implement
[`Scrollable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Scrollable), the scrolled window will add the child to
a [`Viewport`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Viewport) and then set the viewport as the child.

has-frame.brief: Whether to draw a frame around the contents.
has-frame.md: Whether to draw a frame around the contents.

hscrollbar-policy.brief: When the horizontal scrollbar is displayed.
hscrollbar-policy.md:
When the horizontal scrollbar is displayed.

Use [`ScrolledWindow.set_policy()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:set_policy) to set
this property.

kinetic-scrolling.brief: Whether kinetic scrolling is enabled or not.
kinetic-scrolling.md:
Whether kinetic scrolling is enabled or not.

Kinetic scrolling only applies to devices with source %GDK_SOURCE_TOUCHSCREEN.

overlay-scrolling.brief: Whether overlay scrolling is enabled or not.
overlay-scrolling.md:
Whether overlay scrolling is enabled or not.

If it is, the scrollbars are only added as traditional widgets
when a mouse is present. Otherwise, they are overlaid on top of
the content, as narrow indicators.

Note that overlay scrolling can also be globally disabled, with
the [`Settings:gtk-overlay-scrolling`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Settings#property:gtk-overlay-scrolling) setting.

propagate-natural-height.brief: Whether the natural height of the child should be calculated and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural height.
propagate-natural-height.md:
Whether the natural height of the child should be calculated and propagated
through the scrolled window’s requested natural height.

This is useful in cases where an attempt should be made to allocate exactly
enough space for the natural size of the child.

propagate-natural-width.brief: Whether the natural width of the child should be calculated and propagated through the scrolled window’s requested natural width.
propagate-natural-width.md:
Whether the natural width of the child should be calculated and propagated
through the scrolled window’s requested natural width.

This is useful in cases where an attempt should be made to allocate exactly
enough space for the natural size of the child.

vscrollbar-policy.brief: When the vertical scrollbar is displayed.
vscrollbar-policy.md:
When the vertical scrollbar is displayed.

Use [`ScrolledWindow.set_policy()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#method:set_policy) to set
this property.

window-placement.brief: Where the contents are located with respect to the scrollbars.
window-placement.md: Where the contents are located with respect to the scrollbars.

edge-overshot.brief: Emitted whenever user initiated scrolling makes the scrolled window firmly surpass the limits defined by the adjustment in that orientation.
edge-overshot.md:
Emitted whenever user initiated scrolling makes the scrolled
window firmly surpass the limits defined by the adjustment
in that orientation.

A similar behavior without edge resistance is provided by the
[`ScrolledWindow::edge-reached`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#event:edge-reached) signal.

Note: The `pos` argument is LTR/RTL aware, so callers should be
aware too if intending to provide behavior on horizontal edges.

edge-reached.brief: Emitted whenever user-initiated scrolling makes the scrolled window exactly reach the lower or upper limits defined by the adjustment in that orientation.
edge-reached.md:
Emitted whenever user-initiated scrolling makes the scrolled
window exactly reach the lower or upper limits defined by the
adjustment in that orientation.

A similar behavior with edge resistance is provided by the
[`ScrolledWindow::edge-overshot`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ScrolledWindow#event:edge-overshot) signal.

Note: The `pos` argument is LTR/RTL aware, so callers should be
aware too if intending to provide behavior on horizontal edges.

move-focus-out.brief: Emitted when focus is moved away from the scrolled window by a keybinding.
move-focus-out.md:
Emitted when focus is moved away from the scrolled window by a
keybinding.

This is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

The default bindings for this signal are
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> to move forward and
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>` to move backward.

scroll-child.brief: Emitted when a keybinding that scrolls is pressed.
scroll-child.md:
Emitted when a keybinding that scrolls is pressed.

This is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

The horizontal or vertical adjustment is updated which triggers a
signal that the scrolled window’s child may listen to and scroll itself.
